script: stop 1 card 2, answer 2: copies a Prep line word for word

findings.problem: "You don't climb back into the oven once the batch is out and cooling!" fails the joke logic test in papa-dorin.md: neither a baker nor a cookie stamper was ever inside the oven to climb back into it, cookies don't climb, and climbing into an oven is jarring imagery.

"so he's picking a picture everybody could feel" adds Paul's reason for choosing the image, which the text never states (Reasons rule in papa-dorin.md), and "once more." places a period inside quotation marks around Bible words where BSB Galatians 5:1 has none.
Flat, generic study-guide prose ("Paul really does say it, friend... Paul's warning is right there in the verse, so this one is True.") with none of Papa Dorin's lively voice, warmth, or humor.
"That's why he signs his name first" states why Paul names himself in Galatians 5:2, adding a reason the text does not give (and treating "I, Paul, tell you" as literally signing his name).
"That's why he puts his own name on the line before saying it" states Paul's reason as fact when the text does not give why he says "I, Paul." The tone is also flat and generic.
"testify," places a comma inside quotation marks around a Bible word where BSB Galatians 5:3 has none ("Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included").

Galatians 5:3 concerns circumcision (the body's private matters, which papa-dorin.md says has no joke), and "Take one piece and you've signed up for the whole batch" right after "gets himself circumcised" reads awkwardly.
The quote from Galatians 5:4 cuts off mid-sentence before "; you have fallen away from grace." without showing "…", and "he chose it on purpose" adds authorial intent not stated in the text.
The quote from Galatians 5:4 replaces the BSB semicolon after "Christ;" with a period inside the quotation marks and cuts off mid-verse without "…". The delivery is also flat and generic.

"have been severed from Christ." replaces the BSB semicolon in Galatians 5:4 with a period inside the quotation marks and cuts off mid-verse without "…", and "they drifted from it" softens "have fallen away from grace."
"eagerly," puts a comma inside quotation marks around a Bible word where BSB Galatians 5:5 has none.
Stiff, textbook delivery ("Faith is the word... Notice the two parts: faith, and the Spirit.") misses an easy warm or funny moment about eagerly waiting.
Robotic tutor phrasing ("So law can't be the answer here... Faith is what fills the blank.") lacks Papa Dorin's warmth and personality.
Calling "effort" "Close to the feeling" of Galatians 5:5 misrepresents the passage, which contrasts human effort and law-keeping with waiting by faith through the Spirit.
Flat, generic quiz-tutor phrasing ("Faith goes in the blank.") does not sound like Papa Dorin.

Calling circumcision and uncircumcision "the old marks" is inaccurate because uncircumcision is not a mark, and "in Christ Jesus," adds a comma inside the quotation marks that is not in BSB Galatians 5:6.
Flat, generic summary ending in "That's the answer, friend." with none of Papa Dorin's character or warmth.
Dry, generic explanation with no Papa Dorin personality or storytelling warmth.
Flat and repetitive: restates Galatians 5:8 three ways with zero Papa Dorin personality or humor.
Bare, generic restatement with none of Papa Dorin's voice or humor on a moment where an everyday comparison easily fits.

Galatians 5:9 is literally about a batch of dough, yet Papa Dorin gives a dry dictionary explanation ("Leaven is what makes dough rise... His picture is a small bit working through all of it.") with no humor or bakery life.
Flat, repetitive prose on a literal dough verse where Papa Dorin's bakery humor and personality belong.
Thin, generic explanation (including the verbless fragment "A little bit, but the whole batch.") that misses an obvious chance for Papa Dorin's bakery voice on a dough verse.
Circular, robotic filler ("Notice the 'whoever he may be.' Paul says it of the one troubling them, whoever that is.") does not sound like Papa Dorin.
Stiff, generic three-sentence restatement ("And the 'whoever he may be' makes it plain who it covers.") lacking Papa Dorin's voice.
"No promotion here, friend." is a verbless fragment, leaving only 2 full sentences instead of the 3 to 5 sentences required by answer-explanations.md.
Flat, generic study-note phrasing ("Then he tells them what to do with it.") without Papa Dorin's voice.
Lifeless restatement ("So the answer is True. The warning comes right after the call to freedom.") with none of Papa Dorin's warmth or character.
States the Bible fact "That's a command in the law" (Remember the Sabbath day, Exodus 20:8) without carrying its Scripture reference, breaking the References rule in papa-dorin.md.
Dry, textbook phrasing ("Paul points to love of neighbor.") with none of Papa Dorin's personality.
Refers to "Honor your father and mother" as a Bible command without giving its Scripture reference (Exodus 20:12).
Flat, repetitive filler ("not the one Paul picks... That's the single decree he names.") with no Papa Dorin warmth or humor.
Flat, generic prose ("Biting and devouring leads to being consumed."), and calling "scattered" "Close in feel" to "consumed" doesn't fit Paul's image of devouring each other until nothing is left.
"Not shamed, friend." is a short fragment without a verb, leaving only 2 full sentences instead of the 3 to 5 sentences required by answer-explanations.md.
Dry, generic explanation lacking Papa Dorin's voice and warmth.
